How to play

Aim by swiping on the table: the cue turns around the cue ball. Rather point at a spot? Pick Tap & drag in Controls. The dotted line shows where the cue ball goes and where the object ball will travel.

Shoot by putting your finger on the cue stick, pulling it back and letting go. Further pull means a harder shot. You can also pull the power bar down. With a mouse or touchpad, just move the pointer to aim, then press, drag back and let go.

Aiming wheel: roll the ribbed wheel beside the power bar for tiny, precise turns.

Spin: tap the little cue ball to open the big spin view, then drag the red dot: top for follow, bottom for screw back, sides for side spin.

Controls in the menu sets the aiming style, cue sensitivity, tap to aim, the aiming wheel, tap to shoot and which side the power bar sits on.

Shot clock: you have 35 seconds for each shot. If time runs out, it is a foul and the other player gets ball in hand.

Fouls give your opponent ball in hand: scratching, hitting the wrong ball first, hitting nothing, or no ball reaching a rail after contact. Sink the 8 early and you lose.

Keyboard: A and D aim (hold Shift to turn faster), the arrow keys move the spin dot, W opens the spin view, E picks a cue. Hold Space to power up, then let go to shoot. Esc pauses.

Skill shots like banks, kicks, combos and a break and run pay bonus coins and XP in every match. See the full list under “Skill shot bonuses”.

Skills from the Skills shop give you a few special shots each game: tap the lightning button next to the spin ball on your turn.

Fair play: cues, tables, ball designs and avatars only change the look. They never make shots easier.

Auto keeps everything on and only trims a few effects if the game keeps stuttering. Smooth is fastest, for slower laptops and Chromebooks: a still table, no screen shake and fewer effects. Best keeps every effect on. The picture always stays sharp.

Controls

Aiming

Mouse & touchpad

Cue sensitivity

How fast the cue turns when you swipe on the table. Slow makes long shots easier to line up.

Tap to aim

With Swipe aiming, tap the left or right side of the table to nudge the cue one tiny step.

Aiming wheel

A wheel beside the power bar that turns the cue very slowly for precise shots.

Tap to shoot

Off: you have to drag the power bar, so brushing it never fires a weak shot. On: tap the bar to shoot at that power.

Power bar side
How the controls work

Touch: swipe on the table to turn the cue (or pick Tap & drag to point it). Put your finger on the cue stick, pull it back and let go to shoot; the power bar works too. Tap the little cue ball to open the big spin view and drag the red dot.

Mouse or touchpad: move the pointer and the cue follows it, no clicking needed. Click once to lock the aim (the aiming wheel and the A and D keys lock it too). Press anywhere on the table, drag back and let go to shoot. You can also drag the power bar.

Keyboard: A and D aim (hold Shift to turn faster), the arrow keys move the spin dot, W opens the spin view, E picks a cue, hold Space to power up and let go to shoot, Esc pauses.

Unlock a skill once with coins and it comes to every match. Tap the lightning button next to the spin ball on your turn to use one. Each skill has a few uses per game, and upgrades add more. Computer players never use skills.

Daily missions

Three new missions every day, all done by playing. Progress shows up during matches. Rewards arrive the moment you finish. Missing a day never costs you anything.
